The main celebration of the trip takes place in Rio de Janeiro. Thousands of people dressed in white gather on the beach, sending flowers and small boats with offerings to Iemanjá out to sea. Fireworks light up the water, and free concerts take place on stages along the beach. After the celebrations, the route heads for the Andes, with ancient sites, highland roads, the Hiram Bingham train, the Uros and Taquile islands, the Pacific Ocean and a flight over the Nazca Lines still ahead.

## New Year in Brazil and Peru

The festive part of the trip brings together two different traditions. In Rio, New Year is celebrated on the oceanfront. People gather in the open air, wear white, send flowers out onto the water and welcome midnight with fireworks over Copacabana.

In Peru, New Year customs draw on ancient Andean beliefs and modern urban celebrations. Processions and cleansing rituals take place in Cusco and around Machu Picchu. One local custom is to walk around the main square for good luck in the new year. Around Lake Titicaca, bonfires feature in festive traditions as symbols of light, peace and prosperity.

This part of the itinerary takes you from the lively celebrations by the ocean to quieter Andean towns and sacred sites. After Rio, the trip crosses several of Peru's landscapes, from the Pacific coast and the Andean valleys to the highlands, Lake Titicaca and the desert of Paracas.

In your free time, you can choose from separate tours of the city and its natural areas.

## What you'll remember from the trip

In Brazil, there is Copacabana dressed in white on New Year's Eve, fireworks over the ocean, Sugarloaf Mountain, Corcovado, the Selarón Steps, the Tijuca Forest and the chance to see Rio from the air.

In Peru, the highlights change almost every day: colonial Lima, the animals of Awanakancha, the Pisac market, the salt terraces of Maras, the circles of Moray, the Hiram Bingham train, Machu Picchu, the stone walls of Cusco, the Route of the Sun, Lake Titicaca high in the Andes, the Uros reed islands, the weaving traditions of Taquile, the Paracas desert and the mysterious Nazca Lines.

The itinerary pairs Rio's New Year celebrations with an extensive journey through Peru, with upscale hotels, private transfers on key legs, English-speaking guides and several days when the journey itself is part of the experience.
